Article Title: Akhilesh, Dimple Yadav to visit Ram Temple in Ayodhya on Dec 12, says SP leader Pandey ahead of UP polls
Article Text:
Akhilesh's planned Ayodhya visit comes amid renewed political focus on the temple town ahead of the 2027 UP polls

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and his wife Dimple Yadav will visit the Ram Temple and Hanumangarhi in Ayodhya on December 12, former SP MLA Pawan Pandey announced on Saturday, ahead of the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections scheduled for early 2027."Both Akhilesh ji and his wife Dimple Yadav ji will visit Ram Temple and also visit the Hanumangarhi temple at Ayodhya on December 12," Pandey, who has been renominated as the SP candidate from Ayodhya, told reporters.The proposed visit will be Akhilesh's first to the Ram Temple since its inauguration in January 2024. The SP chief has faced repeated criticism from the BJP over not visiting the temple, with the ruling party accusing him of pursuing appeasement politics.Pandey said Akhilesh would visit Ayodhya with his family, meet saints and seek their blessings. The announcement comes as the BJP government led by Yogi Adityanath prepares for Deepotsav celebrations in the temple town.Akhilesh has previously said he would visit the Ram Temple after the completion of Kedareshwar Dham, a temple being built by the Samajwadi Party in Etawah.He has also accused the BJP and Sangh organisations of "chanda chori" in connection with the Ram Temple.The proposed visit comes amid the political contest over Ayodhya ahead of the 2027 polls. The BJP has repeatedly invoked the police firing on karsevaks in the 1990s, when Mulayam Singh Yadav was Uttar Pradesh chief minister, while targeting the SP.
Article Summary: Akhilesh Yadav and his wife Dimple Yadav will visit the Ram Temple and Hanumangarhi in Ayodhya on December 12. Former SP MLA Pawan Pandey announced the visit ahead of the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections scheduled for early 2027. Akhilesh has faced repeated criticism from the BJP over not visiting the temple.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday challenged Union home minister Amit Shah to an open debate on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. His video of Amit Shah prompted a sharp response from the BJP , which accused him of circulating a cropped video and lacking preparation on the issue.Addressing Shah directly, Rahul said, "Amit Shah ji, don't confuse Modi ji. Just convince him to have an open debate with me. Any platform, any time. Don't be afraid."Responding to Rahul's remarks, parliamentary affairs minister Pralhad Joshi accused the Congress leader of sharing an edited video of Shah's remarks without the proper context. He said the clip exposed Rahul's "absolute lack of homework on SIR"."Rahul ji, the confusion is clearly yours, not ours!" Joshi said in a post on X.He also questioned Rahul's stance on electoral processes, alleging that the Congress leader accepted them when his party won elections but questioned them after defeats."When you win elections, the electoral process is acceptable; when you lose, the same process suddenly becomes questionable. Is this your understanding of democracy?" Joshi said.Taking a swipe at Rahul's electoral record, the BJP leader pointed out that the Congress lost the 2014, 2019 and 2024 Lok Sabha elections even when no SIR was conducted."You lost the 2014, 2019 and 2024 Lok Sabha elections even when no SIR was conducted. Will you take responsibility for those defeats or blame something else?" he asked.Joshi further said Shah had already challenged Rahul to discuss SIR in Parliament and offered to convene a special session for the purpose."And now, when Home Minister Shri @AmitShah ji has openly challenged you to discuss SIR in Parliament and even offered a special session, why the hesitation. Enough of political theatrics, Rahul ji. Bring your arguments to Parliament and debate with facts," he said.The exchange followed a video clip featuring remarks by Shah in Parliament and at another public address. In the parliamentary remarks, Shah questioned the possibility of holding a discussion on SIR in the House and asked who would be held responsible if questions were raised.Addressing Rahul's demand for a debate with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Shah said the prime minister's presence was not necessary for the discussion."Rahul ji, Modi ji ki zaroorat nahi hai... Hum SIR par charcha ke liye vishesh sansad ka satra bulane ke liye taiyaar hain," Shah said.The edited video juxtaposed Shah's remarks with an earlier statement by Rahul, who had said, "Inko hum matlab pagal kar denge". It ended with Rahul smiling at a press conference, alongside an overlay reading "Confusion mein aa gaye".
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday challenged Union home minister Amit Shah to an open debate on the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. His video of Amit Shah prompted a sharp response from the BJP, which accused him of circulating a cropped video and lacking preparation on the issue.

Article Title: INDIA bloc stages mock arrest of CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Bengaluru protest: Watch
Article Text:
INDIA bloc stages dramatic mock arrest of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over SIR row

NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc on Wednesday held a state-level protest at Freedom Park in Bengaluru, demanding the immediate resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged manipulation of electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.Video footage from the rally showed party workers enacting the arrest of Gyanesh Kumar as part of the demonstration.The protest, which began at 11 am and was scheduled to continue until 2 pm, was organised by the Congress, CPI(M), CPI, CPI(ML) Liberation, Forward Bloc and Samajwadi Party, along with other progressive parties, social organisations and student and youth groups involved in the anti-SIR agitation.The demonstration was presided over by Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister DK Shivakumar, former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) President BK Hariprasad.Multilingual film actor Prakash Raj, CPI(M) state secretary Prakash K, CPI state secretary Sathi Sundaresh, CPI(ML) Liberation state secretary Clifton D'Rozario, Forward Bloc president JR Shivashankar and Samajwadi Party president N Manjappa also participated in the protest.Representatives of various organisations, including Sarvodaya Karnataka, Eddelu Karnataka, the Federation of Dalit Organisations and the Republican Party of India, attended the rally. Police personnel were deployed in adequate numbers at Freedom Park to maintain security and manage the gathering.The protest was held as part of the INDIA bloc's wider agitation against the SIR exercise and its demand for the CEC's resignation. It follows a demonstration organised by the opposition alliance at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on November 1.On Wednesday, Hariprasad said the Bengaluru rally was a continuation of the November 1 protest and that leaders of several INDIA bloc parties had agreed to participate."In continuation of the protest we had on November 1, the entire INDIA bloc alliance is organising a massive protest at Freedom Park in Bengaluru. All our CPI(M), Forward Bloc, Samajwadi Party... and Muslim League leaders have agreed to participate in this," Hariprasad said.He also said the agitation would be extended to districts across Karnataka, with party units asked to organise simultaneous demonstrations at the block level."This protest will continue in Karnataka in almost all districts at the block level. Tomorrow, we have requested all our district units to simultaneously hold protests against SIR and Gyanesh Kumar and demand his resignation," he said.
Article Summary: The protest was held as part of the INDIA bloc's wider agitation against the SIR exercise and its demand for the CEC's resignation. The demonstration was presided over by Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister DK Shivakumar, former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee President BK Hariprasad.

NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Saturday reacted to the alleged attack on Trinamool Congress (TMC) national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee ’s residence, accusing the BJP of disrupting traditional Kali Puja celebrations in the locality ahead of Kali Puja and Diwali.Speaking in Kolkata, Mamata questioned the disturbance caused in an area that serves as a traditional route for several Kali Puja processions.“Tomorrow is Kali Puja and Diwali. Last night, at 2:00 AM, an attack was carried out at Abhishek Banerjee’s house. This is our locality, a route through which many processions of Goddess Kali pass. Why are you causing such a disturbance?” she said.She also alleged that permissions for traditional pujas had been revoked while new celebrations were being allowed, and claimed that local clubs had been prevented from carrying out their activities the previous night.“We are part of the 'INDIA' alliance, and this is the reason for their anger,” Mamata added, alleging that the political opposition was behind the hostility.In another statement, Mamata said: “If you have the courage to use a bulldozer, why do you come here at 3:00 in the morning with a gang of thugs to attack a Kali Puja celebration?”The remarks came after Abhishek Banerjee alleged that BJP workers attacked his residence around 2am on Saturday, accusing Kolkata Police of failing to prevent the incident.In a post on X, Abhishek claimed the attack took place shortly after he released a video showing unidentified individuals allegedly conducting reconnaissance of his office and residence. He described it as the seventh attempt on his life in the past six months and accused the police and judiciary of failing to act.The BJP rejected the allegations, with West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh dismissing them as an attempt to mislead people.“This is the first time we’ve seen a politician’s birthday being celebrated on the footpath. If someone creates a disturbance, there is bound to be a backlash. Besides, who has the time to kill Abhishek Banerjee? There is nothing left for them to say or do, so they are attempting to mislead people by bringing up this issue,” Ghosh said.

Article Title: 'Directed at Delhi govt officials': Court dismisses plea seeking FIR against CM Rekha Gupta over Lord Hanuman remark
Article Text:

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: In a relief to Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta, a city court on Friday dismissed a complaint seeking registration of an FIR against her for allegedly comparing Delhi government officials to Lord Hanuman.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar dismissed the application filed by complainant Ram Niwas Sharma, observing that Gupta's remarks appeared to be directed at the officials and their performance."The comparison between the officials of the Delhi government and Lord Hanuman by the speaker appears to be directed towards the officials and their performance, and at this stage, it can be said that the material does not prima facie disclose the deliberate and malicious intention to insult religion or religious beliefs, an essential ingredient of Section 299 of the BNS," the court said in its order, referring to Gupta.Sharma had sought registration of an FIR under Section 299 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which deals with deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings.The magistrate further noted that Gupta's speech was already on record and, therefore, did not require a police investigation to obtain evidence that was readily accessible to the complainant."The speech delivered by the serving CM... on September 23, 2025 during an official government function organised at Kashmere Gate ISBT, Delhi, for inaugurating DTC bus services from Delhi to Baraut (Uttar Pradesh), which is the genesis of the present complaint, was also procured by the police from the Directorate of Information and Publicity and has been filed on record along with the Action Taken Report," the court said."The identity of the speaker, date, venue and words complained of are ascertainable from the material already collected and placed on record. No specific evidence which is beyond the reach of the complainant or which necessarily requires police investigation has been identified/highlighted by the complainant," it added.The Delhi Police had submitted a report on October 15, stating that there were no grounds to register a case as no cognisable offence was made out.
Article Summary: A city court on Friday dismissed a complaint seeking registration of an FIR against Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta. The complaint was filed by Ram Niwas Sharma, who accused Gupta of comparing Delhi government officials to Lord Hanuman. The court noted that Gupta's remarks appeared to be directed at the officials and their performance.

Article Title: ‘No malicious intent’: Court junks plea for FIR against CM over her remarks
Article Text:
New Delhi:

ki kripa se saare kaam ho rahe hain





A Delhi court Friday dismissed a complaint seeking action against chief minister Rekha Gupta over her alleged remark comparing govt officials to Lord Hanuman during an official programme.Additional chief judicial magistrate Ashwani Panwar held that the material did not prima facie establish the deliberate and malicious intention required to constitute an offence under Section 299 of BNS (deliberate acts intended to outrage religious feelings).Panwar also observed that Gupta’s remarks, made at an official govt programme at Kashmere Gate ISBT on Sept 23, 2025, when viewed in their entirety, were directed at the” work performance of govt officials and did not indicate an intention to insult Lord Hanuman or outrage religious sentiments.”The complaint, filed by one Ram Niwas Sharma under BNSS, alleged that the CM’s remarks warranted legal action. Panwar clarified that an FIR under Section 175(3) of BNSS is warranted primarily when police assistance or custodial interrogation is required to unearth evidence beyond the complainant’s reach. “The essential material is already on record and the evidence can be led directly before the court by summoning witnesses,” the magistrate observed.The court noted that the complainant had already placed on record an official video transcript, a certificate under Section 63(4)(C) of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023, and details of the speaker’s identity, venue and date.In an action taken report (ATR) filed by Kashmere Gate police station, police had also concluded that no cognisable offence was made out. It described Gupta’s address as “encouraging and appreciative,” noting that she had praised the officials’ work, commitment and dedication by positively comparing them with Lord Hanuman.The report also pointed out that the complainant had selectively omitted portions of the speech, including her remark, “Hanuman ji”. It termed the complaint an “orchestrated political vendetta”.The court also found no prima facie basis for the allegations against the CM, but granted the petitioner liberty to proceed with the private complaint under Section 223 of BNSS and provide evidence before the magistrate.
Article Summary: A Delhi court dismissed a complaint seeking action against chief minister Rekha Gupta over her alleged remark comparing govt officials to Lord Hanuman.Additional chief judicial magistrate Ashwani Panwar held that the material did not prima facie establish the deliberate and malicious intention required to constitute an offence.

Article Title: Not a relative: HC quashes dowry case against woman accused only of affair with complainant’s husband
Article Text:
File photo : Aurangabad bench of Bombay High Court File photo - High court.(With Akhef's story) Aurangabad,TOI,Photo by Snehil Sakhare

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Aurangabad bench of Bombay high court has quashed a criminal case against a Bengaluru-based woman who was arraigned in a matrimonial dispute solely on the allegation that she was in an illicit relationship with the complainant’s husband.Justice Sushil M Ghodeswar, in an order passed last week, allowed the woman’s plea under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, challenging an FIR registered at Chakur police station in Latur district on June 4, 2020. The FIR had invoked sections 498-A (cruelty by husband or relatives), 323 (voluntarily causing hurt), 504 (intentional insult) and 506 (criminal intimidation), read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code (IPC).According to the complainant, who got married on May 27, 2013, she was harassed by her husband and in-laws over a demand of Rs 50 lakh to buy a flat in Bengaluru. She alleged that her husband introduced the Bengaluru woman as his friend despite being in an illicit relationship with her, assaulted her in a drunken state on March 11, 2020, and that her in-laws forced her to undergo an abortion in 2017.After a chargesheet was filed, the Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC), Chakur, took cognisance of the case on Dec 21, 2024, and issued summons to all accused, including the Bengaluru woman.Appearing for the applicant (Bengaluru woman), advocate Ganesh Gadhe argued that she was neither related to the husband nor his family and was residing in Bengaluru. He contended that the allegations against her were vague, unsupported by any specific overt act, and that none of the witness statements implicated her in any offence.Assistant public prosecutor M A Aher, and advocate H B Nandagawale represented the complainant and argued that the chargesheet contained sufficient material and that the Bengaluru woman’s role should be tested during trial.HC relied on Supreme Court’s rulings in State of Haryana vs Bhajan Lal (1992), U Suvetha vs State (2009), and Dechamma I M @ Dechamma Koushik vs State of Karnataka (Dec 4, 2024). The apex court had held that a woman with whom a husband allegedly had an extra-marital relationship was not a ‘relative’ of the husband under Section 498-A.After examining the FIR and witness statements, Justice Ghodeswar observed that the complaint was “lodged as a result of matrimonial differences” between the complainant and her husband. “The only allegation against the applicant is that she was in an illicit relationship with the husband. The applicant is neither related to the husband by blood nor by marriage, and therefore, she cannot be said to be a ‘relative’ of the husband so as to attract Section 498-A,” the court said.The judge further noted that the allegations regarding dowry demand, assault and forced abortion were directed against the husband and in-laws, and that “no specific incident, date or overt act” had been attributed to the applicant to attract offences under sections 323, 504 and 506 IPC. “Even if the allegations are taken at their face value, no offence is made out against the applicant,” the high court held.Invoking the need “to prevent abuse of the process of law and to secure the ends of justice,” the court quashed the FIR, the cognisance order and all consequential proceedings against the Bengaluru woman, while allowing the case to continue against the remaining accused.
Article Summary: Bengaluru-based woman was arraigned in a matrimonial dispute solely on the allegation that she was in an illicit relationship with the complainant's husband. Justice Sushil M Ghodeswar, in an order passed last week, allowed the woman’s plea under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.

Article Title: Manoj Jarange conditionally agrees to hand over Rs 500cr audio clip to SIT, seeks written assurance from CM, Dy CM on source’s safety
Article Text:
Manoj jarange

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange has agreed to hand over the original audio clip, in which a purported Rs 500-crore deal to weaken his agitation was discussed, to the special investigation team (SIT).However, he has sought a written assurance from chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde that the person who provided the recording would not face any threat to their life.Jarange said he was ready to share not only the original audio recording but also details of its source and how it reached him. However, he insisted that the government take responsibility for the safety of the person who provided the clip and their family before he disclosed their identity."The CM and deputy CM must give a 100% written assurance that the person who provided the audio clip, as well as their family members, will not face any threat to their lives. The government must take responsibility for their protection," Jarange said while speaking to reporters.He added that he wanted the truth behind the alleged Rs 500-crore transaction to emerge and the main conspirator to be exposed through an impartial investigation.The development came after the three-member SIT, constituted on the directions of CM Fadnavis, formally approached Jarange and handed him a letter seeking the complete audio recording played during his press conference, its original digital data and other supporting evidence.The SIT is headed by senior IPS officer Shailesh Balkawade, additional commissioner of police (crime), Mumbai. The team has been tasked with examining the allegations and establishing the authenticity and origin of the recording.Jarange said he had no objection to submitting the recording to the investigating officers and would cooperate fully with the probe. "I want this matter to reach its logical conclusion. I am ready to hand over the audio clip to the SIT and disclose its original source, including how and through whom it reached me. However, the safety of the person who gave it to me must be guaranteed," he said.The controversy erupted after Jarange played a purported telephone conversation at a press conference, in which claims were made that Rs 500 crore had been routed to him through Shiv Sena MP Shrikant Shinde. The recording triggered a political storm, with leaders of the BJP and the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena trading allegations.Questioning the claims, Jarange had asked whether someone had allegedly collected money in his name, claiming that the amount was meant for him. He had also questioned whether he had received even a single rupee and demanded a high-level inquiry to identify those behind the alleged transaction.The SIT is expected to subject the recording and accompanying digital evidence to forensic examination to establish its authenticity and identify those involved.
Article Summary: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange has agreed to hand over the original audio clip, in which a purported Rs 500-crore deal to weaken his agitation was discussed. He has sought a written assurance from chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde that the person who provided the recording would not face any threat to their life. Jarange said he had no objection to submitting the recording to the investigating officers.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: Civic body’s sanitation workers find pair of severed human legs in garbage bag in Pune’s Pimple Gurav, victim yet to be identified, police launch murder probe
Article Text:
Prima facie, the severed legs appeared to be those of a man, police said

Pune:

TOI





A pair of severed human legs stuffed inside a garbage bag was found in Pimple Gurav on Friday morning, prompting Sangvi police to register a murder case and launch an investigation into the victim’s identity and whereabouts of the remaining body parts.The incident came to light around 10.30am when Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation sanitation workers were collecting garbage in Shrinagar Lane No. 3 near Kate Puram Chowk.“While collecting the waste, they found a garbage bag slightly heavier than usual. When one of them checked the bag, he saw toes of a foot. He alerted his colleagues and informed the police,” senior police inspector Jitendra Koli of Sangvi police toldPolice found two human legs severed below the knees inside the bag. “Prima facie, the severed legs appeared to be those of a man,” the officer said.The severed limbs have been sent for medical examination. A dog squad was called to the spot, but initial efforts yielded no leads. “We will register a case of murder. Our teams have started recovering CCTV footage near the spot to get clues,” Koli said.An officer from the Pimpri Chinchwad crime branch said teams had spread out to search for the remaining body parts and establish the victim's identity. “We are also checking missing persons' complaints registered with Pimpri Chinchwad and Pune police,” the officer said.
Article Summary: A pair of severed human legs were found in a garbage bag in Pimple Gurav on Friday morning. Sangvi police have registered a murder case and launched an investigation into the victim’s identity and whereabouts of the remaining body parts. “Prima facie, the severed legs appeared to be those of a man,” police said.

Article Title: Four held with MD worth Rs2.5 lakh in Bhusawal raid
Article Text:
Nashik:





The Bhusawal Taluka police arrested four people during a late-night raid near Kinhi MIDC on Friday and seized 62.21 grams of mephedrone (MD) worth Rs 2.48 lakh. The police also seized two motorcycles and four cellphones, taking the total value of the confiscated items to over Rs 7.2 lakh.Acting on specific information, a team comprising personnel from the Bhusawal Taluka police and the Local Crime Branch (LCB), led by probationary sub-divisional police officer and in-charge of Bhusawal Taluka police station Prashant Darekar, raided the location at around 2.55am.The police arrested four suspects identified as Rishabh Kunal Khedkar (18), Prathamesh Dilip Awhad (27), Shaikh Afzal Shaikh Rehmatullah (26) and Asgarkhan Anwarkhan (57), all residents of different parts of Bhusawal.During the raid, the police seized 62.21 grams of MD, classified as a commercial quantity, worth Rs 2.48 lakh. They also confiscated two motorcycles valued at Rs 3.25 lakh and four cellphones worth Rs 1.55 lakh.The Bhusawal Taluka police registered a case under relevant sections of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act.SP Shrikant Dhivare told reporters that strict action against drug peddling, storage and transportation across Jalgaon district would be a continuous process to make the district drug-free.Meanwhile, the Jamner police seized over 13kg of ganja from a farm in the taluka. Acting on specific information, a police team raided the farm and found cannabis plants worth over Rs 3.35 lakh.The farm owner fled the spot. The Jamner police have registered a case against the farmer under relevant sections of the NDPS Act and launched a search for him.
Article Summary: The Bhusawal Taluka police arrested four people during a late-night raid near Kinhi MIDC on Friday and seized 62.21 grams of mephedrone (MD) worth Rs 2.48 lakh. The police also seized two motorcycles and four cellphones, taking the total value of the confiscated items to over Rs 7.2 lakh.

Article Title: Nashik Central Jail guard caught with 33 grams of charas, gets bail
Article Text:
Nashik Road Central Prison

Nashik:





A case was registered against a guard posted at Nashik Road Central Jail after he was caught carrying 33 grams of charas during routine frisking in the search room before entering the prison premises on Nov 4.Nashik Road police had arrested the suspect, but a court granted him bail because the contraband fell into a minor category.Another jail guard, Narayan Jaysing Rajput (47), filed a complaint in this regard. Nashik Road police registered a case under sections 20(b), 29, and 8(c) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, along with section 54 of the Prisons Act, 1894.The accused is identified as Ravindra Eknath Patil (35). He was caught around 11.58am during a routine security check conducted for personnel entering the prison.According to the complaint, routine frisking in a search room led to the discovery of the banned narcotic substance. Patil had attached charas on his thighs using adhesive tape in an attempt to smuggle it inside the prison. This, the police suspect, was done for selling it to inmates for financial gains.Following the recovery, Rajput lodged an official complaint on behalf of govt, prompting the police to register a case.The police has appointed inspector Bhubaneshwar Ghandat as an investigating officer in the case.“The accused was found in possession of the contraband by the jail authorities, and they registered the complaint. Following his arrest, Patil was produced before a local court in Nashik. The court subsequently granted him bail because the quantity of the seized contraband fell under the minor category,” Ghandat said.
Article Summary: Nashik Road police had arrested the suspect, but a court granted him bail because the contraband fell into a minor category. Ravindra Eknath Patil (35) was caught around 11.58am during a routine security check conducted for personnel entering the prison.

Article Title: 50% of Rs 35,000cr Kumbh funds being siphoned off: Sapkal alleges corruption in projects
Article Text:
Harshwardhan Sapkal while addressing the news conference here in Nashik on Thursday

Nashik

:





Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal on Thursday accused BJP-led Mahayuti govt of large-scale corruption in development works linked to Simhastha Kumbh Mela in Nashik, alleging that nearly 50% of the Rs 35,000-crore earmarked for the event was being siphoned off.Speaking in Nashik after a review meeting of Congress functionaries from north Maharashtra, Sapkal alleged that expenditure on Kumbh-related infrastructure and facilities was being inflated. “Govt claims that Rs 35,000 crore is being spent on development works in Nashik, but the focus is on making money from these projects,” he said, adding that Rs 22 crore was spent on pandals and Rs 3 crore on a helipad for the recent Kumbh flag-hoisting ceremony, while Rs 350 crore is being spent on CCTV cameras. “There is systematic corruption in the name of development works, with 50% of the funds being siphoned off,” he alleged.Sapkal claimed several projects in Nashik remained incomplete and alleged that bogus work orders were being issued. “Kumbh Mela is a sacred event, but BJP-led Mahayuti govt has not spared even this event from corruption,” he said.The allegations were made after a review meeting attended by senior Congress leader Balasaheb Thorat, MP Shobha Bachhav, AICC secretary B M Sandeep and other party functionaries.Congress leaders said the meeting reviewed issues discussed at an earlier camp of district presidents in Nashik.Separately, Thorat accused Mahayuti govt of trying to weaken the cooperative sector. Referring to developments at Gokul, he alleged that despite a panel led by Congress leader Satej Patil having a clear majority, the election of the chairperson was stalled over quorum-related issues. “BJP is going to any extent to capture power. What it did during the Lok Sabha and assembly elections is now being repeated in the cooperative sector,” Thorat alleged.Thorat also criticised the provision allowing the appointment of four govt-nominated members, claiming it could have far-reaching implications for cooperative institutions across the state.
Article Summary: Harshwardhan Sapkal accused BJP-led Mahayuti govt of large-scale corruption in development works linked to Simhastha Kumbh Mela in Nashik. He alleged that nearly 50% of the Rs 35,000-crore earmarked for the event was being siphoned off.

Article Title: Former flight attendant counselled for abandoning her newborn near CM Vijay’s home
Article Text: Chennai: Neelankarai police identified the 34-year-old woman who abandoned her newborn daughter on a roadside near Chief Minister Vijay’s residence at Kapaleeswarar Nagar, Neelankarai, on Thursday. She was detained for questioning and referred for mental health counseling.Police examined CCTV footage from the locality and identified the woman, who lives in the neighbourhood. She reportedly delivered the baby girl at her house two days earlier. As her parents refused to keep the baby, she initially considered leaving her at a nearby cremation ground. But later, she abandoned her on the roadside. Police said she declined to take custody of the infant.Residents who were walking near the rear of the chief minister’s house on Fourth Main Road heard an infant crying and found the newborn with her umbilical cord still attached. They alerted the police, who rescued the baby and took her to a private hospital. She was later shifted to the Govt Institute of Child Health and Hospital for Children in Egmore.Doctors said the infant was stable and receiving treatment. Child Welfare Committee arranged for her care through an orphanage.Neelankarai police registered the Community Service Register (CSR) and are questioning the woman’s parents.
Article Summary: Neelankarai police identified the 34-year-old woman who abandoned her newborn daughter on a roadside near Chief Minister Vijay’s residence. She was detained for questioning and referred for mental health counseling. Police said she declined to take custody of the infant.

Article Title: Woman booked for duping Coimbatore rifle shooting coach of Rs 16 lakh
Article Text: COIMBATORE: The Singanallur police in Coimbatore have registered a case based on a complaint filed by a female rifle shooting coach who alleged that a woman had cheated her of Rs 16 lakh by promising to settle a land dispute using her political influence.The complainant, R Anu Prabha, 30, of Nanjappa Nagar in Singanallur is a coach at a Rifle Academy near Kuniyamuthur. According to the complaint, her mother, Rajeswari, owns 20 cents of land at Kannampalayam village in Sulur taluk. However, a civil dispute is pending in connection with the property.In 2024, V G Dhanalakshmi , the mother of one of the students at the rifle academy, approached Anu Prabha and promised to resolve the land dispute by using her political influence. Trusting her assurance, Anu Prabha paid her a total of Rs 16 lakh in several instalments. The amount included Rs 10.95 lakh in cash and Rs 5.05 transferred through UPI.However, Dhanalakshmi failed to resolve the dispute or return the money. When Anu Prabha demanded repayment, the woman reportedly issued cheques, which were subsequently dishonoured due to insufficient funds. The complainant further alleged that the money was used by Dhanalakshmi to produce a film.She lodged a complaint with the Singanallur police on Wednesday, and police registered a case under sections 316(2) and 318(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and began an investigation.
Article Summary: The complainant, R Anu Prabha, 30, of Nanjappa Nagar in Singanallur is a coach at a Rifle Academy near Kuniyamuthur. According to the complaint, her mother, Rajeswari, owns 20 cents of land at Kannampalayam village in Sulur taluk. A civil dispute is pending in connection with the property.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: AIADMK ex-deputy mayor held in TVK MLA’s ₹30Cr bribe offer charge
Article Text:
Madurai City Central Crime Branch police arresting AIADMK functionary and former deputy mayor P M Mannan on friday





Madurai: AIADMK functionary and former Madurai deputy mayor P M Mannan was arrested on Friday for allegedly offering Rs 30 crore to TVK MLA V M S Mustafa to vote against the govt in a proposed no-confidence motion. However, a Madurai court refused to remand him in judicial custody and ordered his release on a personal bond, questioning the circumstances of his arrest.Madurai city central crime branch (CCB) police arrested Mannan after hours of questioning over a complaint lodged by Mustafa, who represents Madurai Central. Police registered a case under Sections 8 and 12 of Prevention of Corruption Act, dealing with bribery of public servants and abetment, and Section 61(2) of BNS for criminal conspiracy.The MLA had alleged on Wednesday that an AIADMK functionary offered him Rs 15 crore upfront and another Rs 15 crore if he voted against the TVK govt during a no-confidence motion. He claimed to possess audio recordings of the conversations and said he had informed the party leadership.Mannan, currently AIADMK deputy propaganda secretary, served as deputy mayor from 2006 to 2011 on a DMK ticket. A close associate of former Union minister M K Alagiri, he was expelled from DMK in 2014, and joined AIADMK in Feb this year.Separately, police questioned Mustafa’s aide Kani Raj for over five hours regarding his alleged communications with Mannan on Oct 31 and Nov 1. Investigators reportedly seized his mobile phone to examine call records and audio evidence. The inquiry sought to establish whether the alleged offer was communicated to Mustafa through his aide.The arrest, however, came under judicial scrutiny when Mannan was produced before district judge S Joseph Joy. The judge asked why police arrested him on Friday when a notice under Section 35(3) of BNS had directed him to appear for questioning at 10am on Saturday, Nov 7.Rejecting the police request for judicial remand, the court directed his release on a personal bond. “I will abide by the court’s order, continue to cooperate with the investigation and appear before CCB on Saturday as directed,” Mannan told reporters.Condemning the arrest, AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami said, “The govt has fabricated a story through Madurai Central MLA Mustafa, arrested our party functionary Mannan and staged yet another political drama. This is shameful.” He accused TVK of previously engaging in horse-trading, including abducting an AMMK legislator to obtain his signature. He also alleged that the govt was attempting to divert attention from discontent among its own MLAs.Former minister Sellur K Raju accused the govt of using the case to divert attention from administrative failures and rising prices of essential commodities. He also questioned the early-morning detention despite Saturday’s summons. “He is neither a terrorist nor a drug smuggler. He has served the people,” he said.
Article Summary: P M Mannan was arrested on Friday for allegedly offering Rs 30 crore to TVK MLA V M S Mustafa to vote against the govt in a proposed no-confidence motion. A Madurai court refused to remand him in judicial custody and ordered his release on a personal bond, questioning the circumstances of his arrest.

Article Title: Murder suspect arrested near Krishnagiri
Article Text: KRISHNAGIRI: The Krishnagiri district police on Saturday arrested a man on charges of murdering a 70- year-old woman in Pannandur village.District superintendent of police GS Anitha said, Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning.During investigations, police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered Chamundeeswari’s house around 1am on Friday with an intention to steal valuables. “Acting on the findings, special police teams launched a search operation and arrested the man within 12 hours of the crime,” the SP said.
Article Summary: Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning. Police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered the house with an intention to steal valuables.

Article Title: 'Developing border areas into vibrant villages': Uttarakhand CM Dhami celebrates Diwali with Garhwal Rifles soldiers
Article Text:
Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami





DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Saturday took part in a Diwali Milan programme with soldiers at the Garhwal Rifles (Garhwal Greeners) training ground in Garhi Cantt, Dehradun, and said border areas of the state were being developed as "Vibrant Villages. "Speaking at the event, Dhami said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had declared that Mana village would no longer be the "last village" of India but its "first village.""Prime Minister Modi visited Gunji, a village near Adi Kailash, and inspired by him, we have now seen roads being constructed. A road has even been built all the way to Lipulekh. Previously, it was argued that building roads would provide an entry point for enemies. In this manner, 60 to 70 years simply slipped by. That system has now been transformed," Dhami said.The chief minister said high-altitude marathons were also being organised on the Prime Minister's inspiration."I recently visited Adi Kailash, where an 'Adi Kailash Run' was held in Gunji village. Furthermore, we are preparing to host a major marathon this May in the Malari and Niti regions. Many such initiatives are underway to develop these border areas into 'Vibrant Villages.'Roads, bridges and tunnels are being constructed, while optical fibre networks and overall connectivity have become significantly stronger than before," he said, adding that this had enhanced the mobility of the armed forces and strengthened communication systems.After the event, Dhami raised the slogan of "Bharat Mata Ki Jai" along with the soldiers in the spirit of patriotism.Speaking to reporters, Dhami hailed the efforts of soldiers at the borders."Our global identity is growing, and our armed forces have contributed tremendously to this. It is solely due to their contribution that we can celebrate all our festivals today. Our borders are secure, our nation is safe. On this occasion, I extend my heartfelt Diwali greetings to all soldiers, all brave personnel, and their families," he said.Earlier on Friday, CM Dhami participated in the Deepawali Milan program at BJP State Office on Balbir Road in Dehradun.On this occasion, the chief minister extended warm Deepawali greetings and best wishes to BJP State President Shri Mahendra Bhatt, along with party office-bearers, organisation members, and party workers.Sharing the joy of the festival with everyone, the chief minister stated that Deepawali symbolises the triumph of light over darkness, truth over falsehood, and hope over despair.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami took part in a Diwali Milan programme with soldiers. He said border areas of the state were being developed as "Vibrant Villages" He said high-altitude marathons were also being organised on the Prime Minister's inspiration.
